claims.statement: The Settings navigation label is Licensing for FPT or GHEC and License for GHES, despite the GHES-named filename. The fragment does not prove license counts, seat entitlement, financial authority or imported-content rights clearance.

The sequence opens Billing and licensing then Licensing to display detailed license usage information. Navigation is not retrieved usage evidence, deduplication, complete seat accounting or authority to change licenses.

The Settings entry is Messages for GHES and Announcement for GHEC. No FPT label is supplied by the conditional; the fragment is not announcement publication, audience validation or permission to send messages.

The migration warning recommends a service account exempt from Entra CAP when using Enterprise Importer for an organization migration from the stated enterprise location, otherwise migration may be blocked. This specialized upstream guidance is not approved bypass policy, proof an exemption is necessary in every context or authority to create one; account selection, compensating controls and security approval remain unresolved. No CAP change or migration was performed.

The Options entry belongs under Policies on GHES and under Settings otherwise. This version-specific navigation supplies no option semantics, policy enforcement, actor authority or saved configuration.

The pinned note says the containing feature becomes available for GHES from version 3.21. The organization-custom-properties filename suggests context but the text does not independently define the feature or claim public-preview status. Historical future availability is not verified installed-version support or activation.
